alt: A table of four car jobs with miles and months since each was done, showing which limit decides and one job with no date.
caption: An example with made-up numbers. Miles or months, whichever comes first.

lines.label: Request
lines.text: An oil change and a tire rotation, nothing else today.

lines.label: Limit
lines.text: Please don't go over $250 without calling me first.

lines.label: Extras
lines.text: Text me the price in writing before you start.

alt: A card with three lines to say at a repair shop: the job you are requesting, a spending limit and a request for written prices.
caption: Three sentences to say before the keys change hands. The amounts are examples.

items: Ask the seller for receipts and shop names
Write down the odometer and date
Check the VIN for open recalls

alt: A five-item checklist for the first week with a used car that has no service records, from asking the seller to starting a log.
caption: Five steps for a car that came with no paperwork.

alt: A sample car maintenance log with three lines, each showing a date, an odometer reading in miles and the work done.
caption: An example log. Date, miles and what was done on every line.

pieces.text: Say what you can back up. Leave out what you cannot.

alt: A blank service record page with fields for date, miles, what was done, who did it and notes, beside a note to include only what you can back up.
caption: The shape of a record to print for a buyer. Keep receipts separately.

pieces.text: Towing, short trips, dust, heat or cold: check what the manual says for them.

alt: A blank three-row table with job, miles and months columns to fill in from the owner's manual, and a note about harder driving conditions.
caption: A page to copy your manual's intervals onto, once. Leave a column blank if the manual does.

pieces.text: Check the emergency kit is in the car and complete.

alt: A winter car checklist covering battery, tires, wiper blades, washer fluid and lights, with a note to check the emergency kit is complete.
caption: Five checks plus the emergency kit. Note the date, even if nothing needed doing.

pieces.title: Name or plate at the top

pieces.text: Look at both cars together, so you can see which one needs you.

alt: A blank one-page record for a single car with name or plate, job, miles, insurance and registration dates, and a note to review both cars monthly.
caption: Keep each car's record on its own page, and check both together.

items: Tire size and oil on one card

alt: Two checklist cards, one listing what to keep in a glove box such as registration and proof of insurance, and one listing what to leave at home.
caption: Keep the details in the car and the originals at home.

pieces.text: Look six weeks ahead, once a month.

alt: A small table of car registration and insurance dates with an act-by date six weeks earlier, and a note to look six weeks ahead once a month.
caption: An example tracker with made-up dates.

steps.what: Match the VIN, count the keys

pieces.text: Dashboard, door jamb and title should all match.

alt: A timeline of the first week with a new car, from calling the insurer to setting up the glove box, and a note to match the VIN in three places.
caption: The order that keeps the hard-to-fix things first.
